title: Carbon Copy at the Border
story: At the land border, Pavel was sent back for a second copy of the customs form he had already filled. The officer refused a photograph, because the carbon copy had to travel with the luggage. Pavel rewrote every line from memory and checked the totals. The delay cost him the early bus, yet both sheets were stamped. He later kept a blank form in his coat.

vocabulary.definition: The official check on goods people carry across a border
The duplicate sheet made to travel with the bags
The final amounts written on the form
Marked with an official stamp of approval
Empty, with nothing written on it yet

quiz.question: Why did the officer refuse a photograph of the form?
options: The carbon copy had to travel with the luggage
Pavel had already left on the early bus
The totals on the first form were wrong
Blank forms were no longer issued there
quiz.correctAnswer: The carbon copy had to travel with the luggage
quiz.explanation: The officer refused a photograph because the carbon copy had to go with the luggage.
quiz.supportingSentence: The officer refused a photograph, because the carbon copy had to travel with the luggage.

quiz.question: What did the delay cost Pavel?
options: The early bus
His luggage and his coat
The stamp on both sheets
A photograph of the officer
quiz.explanation: The delay cost him the early bus, even though both sheets were stamped.
quiz.supportingSentence: The delay cost him the early bus, yet both sheets were stamped.

quiz.question: What does the blank form in his coat suggest?
options: He meant to avoid another delay over a missing copy
He hoped to be hired as a customs officer
He no longer trusted any stamped sheet
He expected the bus company to supply forms
quiz.correctAnswer: He meant to avoid another delay over a missing copy
quiz.explanation: After losing the early bus for lack of a second copy, keeping a blank form shows he was preparing for the next border.
quiz.supportingSentence: He later kept a blank form in his coat.

quiz.question: What is a carbon copy in this passage?
options: A duplicate sheet that had to go with the bags
A photograph stored on a phone
An official stamp on a bus ticket
A total rewritten from memory
quiz.correctAnswer: A duplicate sheet that had to go with the bags
quiz.explanation: The carbon copy is the second sheet that had to travel with the luggage.
quiz.supportingSentence: The officer refused a photograph, because the carbon copy had to travel with the luggage.

quiz.question: Why does the writer say Pavel rewrote the form from memory?
options: To show he did not have the first copy in his hands
To prove the totals had been false
To suggest the officer had lost the luggage
To argue that borders should ban paper
quiz.correctAnswer: To show he did not have the first copy in his hands
quiz.explanation: Rewriting from memory shows the original form was not with him when he was sent back.
quiz.supportingSentence: Pavel rewrote every line from memory and checked the totals.
